findings.issue: P122.10 says a save that redacts a value says so in a journal row, but only the _panel_write route (_atomic_write_json, save_in_layout) journals. Other plan writers reach the scrubbing atomic_write_json / save_sharded / save_single_file / save_plan_json and drop the returned pointers: _proposals._save, audit-task.py save_single_file (~11451), _evidence_io save_plan_json (1808, 3790), close-phase._revalidated_write, migrate-manifest. The redaction is silent on those paths (the R3 shape).
findings.resolution: Carry with R3: route those writers through _panel_write.save_in_layout, or make the journaling part of the writer's caller contract. Not blocking: the scrub itself is applied on every one of them.

findings.issue: The default scrub also rewrites meta.buildCommands on every CLI write. A gate command naming an interpreter under a home directory becomes the outside token and stops being runnable. When --project-dir is a subdirectory of the checkout, in-repo absolute paths become checkout-root-relative while gate steps run with cwd=project. Both pre-date P122.10 (save_sharded) but the new default widens them to every verb. The journal row names the pointer, so it is not silent, and check-committed-pii would have refused the committed original.
findings.resolution: Next phase: refuse a machine path in a gate entry at the door that sets it, or exempt gate entries from the scrub and let the PII backstop judge them.

findings.issue: scrubbed_values(keep=) has no caller left in scripts/ after the evidence ledger switched to positional steps[i].command; only the mp8 case pins it.
findings.resolution: Delete the parameter and mp8, or leave a note naming the reader it is kept for.

findings.issue: The comment at 1566-1567 still says 'a finding no fix task names'; the predicate is now the verb's, so a finding whose fix task never landed is offered too. The `status not in (accepted-open, carried)` guard restates two of the settled words after open_findings already excluded them. The --answer fix refusal says 'not open: F' for a finding that is open but already names a task, which misleads.
findings.resolution: Reword the comment, drop the redundant guard, and have the refusal say the finding already names a fix task and is dispositioned at sign-off.

intent.note: P122-R1 closed. atomic_write_json now scrubs by default: scrubbed_plan derives the checkout from the target path, and it returns the redacted JSON pointers. raw_atomic_write_json exists by name and is reached only from migrate-json-encoding._locked_migrate, _panel_write.write_config and write_theme. _output.raw_json_writer_violations walks hooks and scripts for any reference, call or alias, with a table of allowed sites. It reports a table row whose site no longer reaches the writer, and reports a tree that defines no raw writer as blind. It has red and allow cases (rj1-rj5), prove-gates rows, and a gate-parity classification. Every CLI plan write (audit-task add/start/done/file-return/signoff, set-priority) goes through _panel_write._atomic_write_json, which journals a plan.redact row naming pointers and never values. repair-commits, repair-tests-add and _proposals reach the scrubbing writers. close-phase's restore puts bytes back via snapshot/restore, not the JSON writer. P122-R11: the ledger keeps only steps[i].command by position, and a nested or top-level command key is scrubbed (sc3). P122-R2 closed. open_findings and SETTLED_STATUS are owned by _manifest_phases. audit-task aliases them and drive-phase.open_findings calls them, so the layer debt is gone. For the three shapes in the description: a finding naming a fix task with no commit is open for both readers; a finding with no fixTask is open; a finding with fixTask plus commit is settled. The driver also refuses --answer fix for a finding that already names a task, because the verb refuses a second task for it, so a drive cannot get stuck. Both outcomes describe their diffs. R3 is only partly met (see low 1), and the earlier lows R3-R11 are not re-opened.
